source_sql: SELECT supplier_id, LOWER(TRIM(invoice_number)) AS normalized_invoice_number, gross_amount, currency_code, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count, ARRAY_AGG(invoice_id ORDER BY invoice_date, invoice_id) AS invoice_ids, MIN(invoice_date) AS first_invoice_date, MAX(invoice_date) AS last_invoice_date FROM invoices WHERE status NOT IN ('voided', 'rejected') AND NULLIF(TRIM(invoice_number), '') IS NOT NULL GROUP BY supplier_id, LOWER(TRIM(invoice_number)), gross_amount, currency_code HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY invoice_count DESC, supplier_id, normalized_invoice_number;
source_question: Find active invoices that may be duplicates because the same supplier submitted the same invoice number, currency, and gross amount more than once. Ignore voided and rejected invoices, and normalize invoice numbers for case and surrounding whitespace.
policy_thresholds: No monetary threshold. A duplicate is flagged when the normalized invoice signature occurs more than once among eligible invoices.
referenced_columns: invoice_id, supplier_id, invoice_number, gross_amount, currency_code, invoice_date, status
detection_logic_summary: Excludes voided and rejected invoices, normalizes nonblank invoice numbers, and flags groups sharing supplier, normalized invoice number, currency, and gross amount when more than one invoice is present.
expected_detection_outcome: One row per repeated supplier, invoice-number, currency, and amount signature, including the invoice count, matching IDs, and earliest and latest invoice dates.
join_and_aggregation_logic: Uses a single-table GROUP BY with COUNT(*) to identify repeated signatures; ARRAY_AGG lists the invoice IDs, while MIN and MAX report the date span. No joins are required.

source_sql: SELECT st.transaction_id, st.supplier_id, st.purchase_order_id, st.category_id, st.channel_code, st.amount, st.transaction_date FROM spend_transactions st WHERE st.status IN ('posted', 'paid') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM approved_procurement_channels ac WHERE ac.category_id = st.category_id AND ac.channel_code = st.channel_code AND ac.valid_from <= st.transaction_date AND (ac.valid_to IS NULL OR st.transaction_date < ac.valid_to)) ORDER BY st.transaction_date, st.transaction_id;
source_question: List posted or paid spend transactions made through a procurement channel that was not approved for the transaction's category on the transaction date. Include the purchase order reference, if present, so reviewers can assess the exception.
policy_thresholds: No monetary threshold. A channel is compliant only when an approval for the transaction's category and channel is effective at the transaction timestamp; valid_to is treated as an exclusive end date, and NULL means no end date.
referenced_columns: transaction_id, supplier_id, purchase_order_id, category_id, channel_code, amount, transaction_date, status, valid_from, valid_to
detection_logic_summary: Filters to posted and paid spend transactions, then uses a correlated NOT EXISTS check to find transactions for which no approved channel record matches both the category and channel and is valid on the transaction timestamp.
expected_detection_outcome: Posted or paid transactions for which no matching, date-effective approved category-channel record exists, with any purchase order reference included in the result.
join_and_aggregation_logic: Uses an anti-semi join implemented with NOT EXISTS against the approved channel table. It returns transaction-level records and performs no grouping or aggregation.

Joins purchase orders to effective-dated category thresholds in a CTE, then self-joins the eligible orders within each seven-day window. Groups by the anchor order and dimensions, counts and sums candidate orders, and aggregates their IDs.
source_sql: WITH eligible_orders AS (SELECT po.po_id, po.supplier_id, po.requester_id, po.cost_center_id, po.category_id, po.created_at, po.amount, pl.threshold_amount FROM purchase_orders po JOIN procurement_policy_thresholds pl ON pl.category_id = po.category_id AND po.created_at >= pl.effective_from AND (pl.effective_to IS NULL OR po.created_at < pl.effective_to) WHERE po.status IN ('approved', 'issued') AND po.amount > 0 AND po.amount < pl.threshold_amount), rolling_groups AS (SELECT anchor.po_id AS anchor_po_id, anchor.supplier_id, anchor.requester_id, anchor.cost_center_id, anchor.category_id, anchor.created_at AS window_start, anchor.threshold_amount, COUNT(candidate.po_id) AS order_count, SUM(candidate.amount) AS window_total, ARRAY_AGG(candidate.po_id ORDER BY candidate.created_at, candidate.po_id) AS purchase_order_ids FROM eligible_orders anchor JOIN eligible_orders candidate ON candidate.supplier_id = anchor.supplier_id AND candidate.requester_id = anchor.requester_id AND candidate.cost_center_id = anchor.cost_center_id AND candidate.category_id = anchor.category_id AND candidate.created_at >= anchor.created_at AND candidate.created_at < anchor.created_at + INTERVAL '7 days' GROUP BY anchor.po_id, anchor.supplier_id, anchor.requester_id, anchor.cost_center_id, anchor.category_id, anchor.created_at, anchor.threshold_amount) SELECT anchor_po_id, supplier_id, requester_id, cost_center_id, category_id, window_start, threshold_amount, order_count, window_total, purchase_order_ids FROM rolling_groups WHERE order_count >= 2 AND window_total > threshold_amount ORDER BY window_total DESC, window_start, anchor_po_id;
source_question: Identify possible split purchases where approved or issued purchase orders from the same supplier, requester, cost center, and category were created within a rolling seven-day window. Flag a group when every order is individually below its applicable category threshold but the group total exceeds the threshold in effect on the first order in that window.
policy_thresholds: Each order must be below its applicable category threshold. The rolling window is seven days from the anchor order's creation timestamp, and the combined total must be strictly greater than the threshold effective for the anchor order.
referenced_columns: po_id, supplier_id, requester_id, cost_center_id, category_id, created_at, amount, status, threshold_amount, effective_from, effective_to
detection_logic_summary: Restricts orders to approved or issued records that are positive and individually below the threshold effective on their creation date. For each eligible order, it checks subsequent orders in the same supplier, requester, cost center, and category combination; it flags windows with at least two orders whose total exceeds the anchor order's threshold.
expected_detection_outcome: One row per anchor order with at least one additional qualifying order in the same rolling window, where the combined amount exceeds the anchor threshold; the row lists the order IDs and aggregate amount.
